title: Flying Mode
paragraphs: "So it's coming my way, huh..."
For some reason, I get the feeling Father has a distant look in his eyes. What's the difference here!? His tolerance for alcohol is perfect, isn't it?
"No, that's not it—I'm actually talking about Mr. Kitamura..."
“It’s true he’s insanely good with his liquor… He got me completely wasted and was still totally fine.”
“Lars-chan, don’t jump on the bandwagon.”
“Father absolutely never gets drunk!”
“It’s true he’s never gotten drunk. But that’s not what Ms. Eclair is getting at, Motoyasu-kun.”
For some reason, Father says this to me in a gentle tone. I’m not quite sure what’s going on.
“We’ve gone way off track, so let’s get back to the point: you’re saying there might be human slaves at Elmero’s house, right?”
“Large Beastmen face certain inconveniences due to their size… I’ve heard that other proud Beastmen, for instance, tend to prefer slaves.”
“Huh.”
“Look, the races walking down that street over there are examples of that. However, I’ve heard that race tends to get along well with their slaves.”

Saying this, Éclair points out the people in the town from the carriage. They’re cat Beastmen. It looks like they’re accompanied by human slaves, but the slaves are well-groomed and seem more like personal porters than anything else. They seem to get along pretty well, actually.
“Cats? Ah, I’ve heard that with cats, rather than saying you ‘keep’ them, it’s more like they’re ‘kept’ or ‘cared for.’ So this is an extension of that, I suppose. They get along well, don’t they?”
“I get the feeling Lord Iwatani might be misunderstanding something, though…”
“Isn’t that a bad analogy?”
“Hmm… Anyway, while Siltvelt takes care not to give Lord Iwatani a bad impression, it is a country where human slaves exist. Please don’t forget that.”
“Yeah. So, Elmero’s family probably uses slaves too, right?”
“Yes… Well, they’re a powerful family within Siltvelt, after all…”
Zou answers in a nervous tone. Does he really not want to go that much?
“Elmero, did you hate it?”
“I’m fine. I figured this was an issue that would come up eventually.”
Come to think of it, he seemed to dislike it when Kou tried to address him by his last name. Does he really hate his family home that much?
“Things are looking a little iffy… but well, we should go pay our respects.”
And so, in that sort of mood, we arrived at Zou’s family home.
“Wow… It’s just as I imagined—or rather, it’s even bigger than I thought. Especially horizontally,”

said Father as he looked out from the carriage at Zou’s family home. Outside the carriage stood a massive mansion set on a vast estate. What’s strange is that it’s long from side to side but doesn’t seem to have a second story. You could call it an Indian-style palace—decorations with that kind of atmosphere could be seen here and there. But the clothing was Western-style, so it had a rather jumbled feel to it. At the entrance to that mansion, several… mammoths were all gathered together, waiting for us.
“Welcome to our Puhant Domain, Shield Hero. Please consider this your home and make yourself at ease,”
said a rather elderly mammoth Beastman, stepping forward. For some reason, his gaze—or rather, the look in his eyes—is sharp. You can really feel his ambition radiating from him.
“I am Lizio Puhant, ruler of the Puhant Domain. It’s a pleasure to meet you.”
“I am Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero. I’m here to pay my respects to the family of Elmero, who serves as my bodyguard, and I’d like to thank you very much for this warm welcome.”

Father returned the greeting on behalf of the family. After that, we each introduced ourselves. Yuki-chan greeted us with an air of nobility, lifting her skirt slightly as she spoke. You’ve gained a lot of experience, Yuki-chan—you’ve truly grown into a lady.
“Well, you must be tired from your journey. Why don’t the Shield Hero and his party take it easy here at the manor to rest up and enjoy our welcome banquet?”
After we finished greeting the head of the household, Mammoth, the one standing next to him—who looked like a female mammoth—made this suggestion.
“Come on, Elmero. Don’t just stand there—show them around, will you?”
“Y-yes… Which rooms should I show them to?”
Prompted by the female mammoth, Zou nodded and asked, looking slightly flustered.
“That’s obvious, isn’t it? The Shield Hero will stay in the head of the household’s room, which was just opened today, and everyone else will stay in the guest quarters.”

As expected, you can tell there’s a certain distance between Zou and the household members. You can tell just from this exchange that he doesn’t understand the house rules. Or rather… since he’s Zou among the Mammoths, he’s completely out of place.
“No, I’d feel too awkward to stay in the head of the household’s room, and I can’t disregard the presence of the bodyguard knights. This time, I’d like to share a room with those accompanying me.”

Father skillfully declines the Mammoth family’s offer to show him around. Their ability to deflect such situations has improved considerably. Well, given how troublesome their first day in Siltvelt was, they’ve probably taken precautions.
“But…”
“Don’t worry about it. We’re the ones causing the trouble here.”
“Hmm… Very well. Elmero, show them the way.”
“Um…”
Zou is looking around nervously, shaking his head from side to side.
“You, really… Never mind. This way.”
And so, we ended up entering Zou’s mansion.

…It feels like we’ve turned into little people inside this mansion. Everything is huge. Not just the great hall—even the hallways are massive, and the rooms are so vast they could easily be mistaken for a gymnasium. On top of that, the mammoths gathered to welcome us are walking around near us, their footsteps thudding continuously.

We were then led to the guest room. It’s huge, as expected. It’s a four-poster bed. You see them in castles too, but this one is incredibly tall. It’s not that the bed is so high we can’t reach it, but it feels like we’re having to scramble up to get in.
“Well then, make yourselves at home… Elmero, please come see me later.”
“Yes. Got it.”
And so, we entered the guest room and settled in to rest.
“Hmm… It does feel like they’re welcoming us, at least.”
“Everything’s so big. We have things like this in certain sections of the castle too, but when everything’s this oversized, it’s kind of inconvenient, isn’t it?”
“You’re right. There seem to be some people who look like servants, but their rooms might actually suit us better.”
“Although they called it a guest room, I suspect it’s actually someone from the family’s room.”
“I see… You’re right; it does feel like a place where people actually live.”
Everything in this room is extra-large. There’s a desk, and there’s a bookshelf, too.
“The door meant for regular people looks like a cat flap—it’s kind of funny, though.”

Father points at the door and smiles. Then he walks over to the window and looks outside. The view is nice. There are large fields and such—the land seems fertile. It’s a bit on the chilly side, though. Looking toward the mountains, it looks like there’s still some snow left.
“Well then, I’ve been called, so I’ll be heading out.”
“Um, this feels like the kind of situation where I’m about to get called out for something—should I go too?”
“No, I think I’ll get more information if I go alone—it’ll help me understand the current situation here.”
Hmm, that’s true—at that rate, he probably won’t slip up in front of Father. In terms of gathering information, Zou might be right. Zou places his hand on the doorknob with a slightly anxious gait.
“Elmero, are you okay?”
Kou asks with concern. Zou turns around and gives a faint smile.
“Yes, I’m fine.”
With a click, Zou left the room.
“I’m kind of worried…”
“That Elmero guy looked like he didn’t even know the layout of his own house.”
“Indeed. If he’d lived here before, I’m sure he’d know it by heart.”

Yuki-chan replies while checking the mansion’s decorations. It’s true—I can’t imagine someone rebuilding such a large mansion over and over again. Not knowing the layout of that mansion is proof that he’s only lived there for a short enough time to not know it.
“…That exchange made it clear at a glance that this wasn’t a familiar home for him.”
“It’s like he’s the only Zou among countless mammoths…”
I feel like I’ve caught a glimpse of the Darkness surrounding the elephant’s house.
“Wasn’t she wandering around because she couldn’t inherit the family estate?”
“That’s what she told her mercenary buddies—though she did go on and on about being a knight.”
“Was she adopted or something?”
“I don’t know the details. I think the quickest way to find out would be to ask her directly.”
“It feels a bit awkward to be asking so many probing questions after coming all this way. Compared to that, it was much easier to ask questions at Lars-chan’s place.”
“Hmm, that’s certainly true. They were good people.”
“Tch!”
Here, the panda clicks its tongue. That’s rather rude.
“…I wonder if Elmero’s okay.”
“Should I go scout things out?”
“I suppose that’s a good idea, but…”
Father turns his attention toward the door.
“They’re standing by under the pretense of providing security. Sneaking past them looks like it’ll be a real hassle.”
“You’re right.”
Was it at that very moment? The sound of a knock on the door echoes through the room.
“Excuse me~”
A mammoth carrying a large pitcher enters the room.
“I brought this so you can drink water anytime. The water here is meltwater from the snow—it’s considered one of the finest in Siltvelt. We’ve also used high-quality ice, so please help yourself.”

This mammoth’s gait—with that slight sway in the hips—somehow resembles a pig strutting like a model. Plus, there’s a strange indentation in its outfit. It’s even wearing false eyelashes… quite a flashy mammoth, indeed.
“Shield Hero~ I’m so sorry about what happened the other day. I really wanted to apologize for what happened back then—”
“Ah, I thought I’d seen you somewhere before—you’re the girl from the castle baths, aren’t you?”
“That’s right. I’m sorry about what happened back then.”
“Yeah. Don’t worry about it. Thanks for bringing me the water.”
“So, Shield Hero, since we’re here, would you like me to show you around the mansion’s garden?　I’ll even wash your back while you’re bathing, okay?”
Father is subtly signaling for her to leave, but the Flashy Mammoth shows no sign of backing down. Finally sensing the tension, Panda and Éclair stepped in between them.
“Excuse me.”
“You’re standing a bit too close, aren’t you? The Shield Hero seems to know he apologized, so isn’t it fine?”
It looks like Keba Mammoth’s eyebrows twitched slightly at Panda’s words.
“As his bodyguards, may we accompany you on the garden tour?”
“……Yes, of course. This way, please.”
It seems Keba Mammoth will be giving us a tour of the garden. It’s quite a large garden, so perhaps they’re growing something there.
“Kou, I’ll wait here so I can explain to Elmero that Iwatani went to the garden when he gets back.”

Kou is making it clear right here that he’s not going. I suppose Kou is worried about the elephant in his own way. All right, I’ll have to do my best, too. I’ll send a subtle signal to Father with my eyes.
“Well then, I’ll stand by as well.”
Yuki-chan must have sensed it too, as she went along with it.
“In that case, I’ll wait in my room, too.”
“Oh? …Well then, count on you, Motoyasu-kun and everyone.”
“Leave it to us.”
Saying things like that, I leaned back against the shadow of the bed to avoid Keba Mammoth’s gaze and struck a salute pose.
“Alright, this way.”
It felt a bit forced, but Kebamammoth didn’t seem to notice. And so, Father and the others were led out to the garden by Kebamammoth.

Just as Kebamammoth was about to open the door and step out, I went into stealth mode and followed right behind Father and the others. Perhaps Kebamammoth wasn’t interested in anyone but Father, because even though I’d vanished from the spot, he didn’t even notice.

And the moment he stepped out of the room, he swiftly moved in the opposite direction from Father and the others. He was heading toward where the elephant’s footsteps had led. However… as expected—or rather, this mansion seems to be quite vast. Reconnaissance is going to be a real pain.
“Hmm…?”
Just then, it looks like one of the mammoths is heading this way. I tried to slip past while still hidden, but I sensed the mammoth was about to turn its head toward me, so I stopped.
“I thought I felt a very slight vibration—have the slaves or servants… disobeyed my orders?”
It muttered something like that while scanning the area with its eyes.
“…Must have been my imagination.”

Perhaps because it couldn’t find anything, the mammoth tilted its head and walked away. It seems to be quite sensitive to footfalls. No, wait—was it vibrations rather than footsteps? It must be sensitive to vibrations coming from the ground.
It seems there are some surprisingly capable creatures out there. This is quite a hassle. If it were a Rival, I’d probably be able to fly past without being noticed.

I’ve got no choice, so I’ll go with the “Flying Mode”—a candidate for my third form that’s still under development. I’ll use my spear to create a Windmill, spin at high speed, and float through the air as I move. Of course, I’m using Magic to cancel out the sound of flight and the wind pressure.
Flutter, flutter, flutter!
